name: tpl-precedence-3-goal
task: Pick up the box in the other room, but do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost) does not capture the full ban. The task forbids dropping the key while the door is closed until it has been opened once, but key_lost only detects losing it while the door is closed; dropping the key while the door is closed does not necessarily make key_lost true if it is picked up again before opening the door. Add a hard Absence for the event that represents dropping the key while the door is closed, if declared, or otherwise use a proposition that captures that event.

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost) forbids key_lost only before the door has first opened. The task forbids dropping the key while the door is closed until it has opened once, so a key_lost event after opening and then closing the door must also be forbidden. Change this to hard Absence(key_lost).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost) does not express the stated ban. `key_lost` is true only when the key is dropped while the door is closed, so the task says never to let that event happen; it does not allow it after the door has opened once. Replace it with hard Absence(key_lost). Keep Existence(target_picked_up).

CHANGES REQUIRED: The hard Absence(key_lost) only forbids losing the key before the door opens; it also forbids it after the door has been opened once. The task says that restriction ends once the door has been opened. Replace it with hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost), which allows key_lost only after door_open has happened. Keep the hard Existence(target_picked_up).

CHANGES REQUIRED: the hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost) allows key_lost after the door has opened once, even if the door is later closed. The task forbids dropping the key while the door is closed until it has been opened once; because key_lost already means the key was dropped while the door is closed, this requires a hard Absence(key_lost), not Precedence. Keep Existence(target_picked_up).

CHANGES REQUIRED: the hard Absence(key_lost) bans losing the key even after the door has opened. The task says not to drop it while the door is closed until the door has been opened once, so use hard Precedence(door_open, key_lost); this ends the ban after the first opening. Keep hard Existence(target_picked_up).

CHANGES REQUIRED: Precedence(door_open, key_lost) forbids key_lost only before the door has first opened. The task says not to drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once; since key_lost is defined as dropping the key while the door is closed, that ban is Absence(key_lost), not Precedence. Replace the Precedence clause with hard Absence(key_lost); keep Existence(target_picked_up).
NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(target_picked_up) requires picking up the box, and Precedence(door_open, key_lost) forbids losing the key before the door has been opened once.

texts: Pick up the mission's box in the other room.
Do not lose the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once.
